Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Malviya, learned counsel for appellants.
 Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the respon
ORDER 1.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 28.01.2015 passed in MACC No.62/2013 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, District Ratlam whereby a total sum of Rs.4,19,000/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

sentences.text: 3. As per the appellants, on 19.03.2013, Ravi Kushwaha, son of appellants 1 and 2 and brother of appellant No.3 along with his son was going on a motorcycle.

At about 2.00 p.m., when he reached Ratlam - Jaora Four Lane road near Ipka Factory, Ratlam respondent No.1 drove Scorpio Jeep bearing registration No.MH-22-Z-3555 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9510 2 MA-866-2015 against his motorcycle as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries and eventually expired.
4. The appellants thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.21,90,000/- to them by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the Amarsingh vs Pankaj on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125300271/
1 appellants as aforesaid.

5. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the income of the deceased which has been assessed at Rs.4,500/- per month is grossly low.
Even if he was to be held to be unemployed then also his income should have been assessed appropriately.
It is further submitted that the multiplier which has been applied is by taking the age of the mother whereas the same ought to have been taken on the basis of the age of the deceased.
It is also submitted that the appellants 1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased were entitled for filial consortium but the same has not been awarded to them.
It is also submitted that the future prospects of rise in income have also not been taken into consideration by the Claims Tribunal.
It is hence submitted that the amount of compensation awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 Insurance Company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellants by the Claims Tribunal in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9510 3 MA-866-2015 7.
I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. Though the appellants have not been able to prove the income of the deceased but from the evidence which is available on record it is evident that he was not unemployed.
He was stated to be doing some work.

He hence at least ought to have been assessed to be an unskilled labourer and in view of the guidelines applicable as on the date of accident which took place in the year 2015 the same deserves to be assessed at Rs.4,945/- per month.

The future prospects of rise in income have also not been taken into consideration by the Claims Tribunal which are mandatorily required to be considered and looking to the age of the deceased they deserve to be taken at 40%.
The multiplier applicable would have been on the basis of the age of the deceased and not on the basis of age of his mother as has been illegally done by the Tribunal.
The multiplier applicable would hence be of 17.

The appellants 1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased and in view of the well settled position of law they would be entitled for award of filial consortium to them though appellant No.3 being the brother would not be so entitled.

9. The amount which the appellants would be entitled on the basis of loss of dependency would hence be Rs.4,945/- per month + 40% future prospects of rise in income multiplied by 12 for making it annually.
The multiplier applicable would be 17 and deduction would be of half since the deceased was unmarried.
Thus under this head the appellants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.7,06,146/-.
Appellants 1 and 2 would be further entitled for award of filial consortium to them in the sum of Rs.80,000/-.
For funeral expenses and loss of estate also the appellants are entitled for a sum of Rs.15,000/- each.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9510 4 MA-866-2015 Amarsingh vs Pankaj on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125300271/

The appellants are entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.8,16,146/- to them by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding them a sum of Rs.4,19,000/-
only.

The appellants are hence held entitled for enhancement in the award of compensation in the sum of Rs.4,19,000/- which shall be paid to them along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
11. The appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.2,00,000/- whereas the enhancement has been made in the sum of Rs.3,97,146/-.
The appellants would hence be required to pay the requisite Court fees on the additional enhanced amount of Rs.1,97,146/- which shall be paid by them within a period of two months.
In case of their failure to pay the Court fees as aforesaid this additional amount of Rs.1,97,146/ shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
12. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
